question.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}-\frac{1}{y}\,dx+\frac{y}{x}\,dy+dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the helix parametrized by $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+t\,k$ for $t\in [0,\pi ].$
question.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z(t)=t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,k \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+k.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}-\frac{1}{y}\,dx+\frac{y}{x}\,dy+dz & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }-\frac{1}{y}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+\frac{y}{x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(-\frac{1}{y}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{y}{x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }-\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)+1\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }2+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =(2t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(2\pi -\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi )+\operatorname{cos}⁡0 \\  & =2(\pi +1)\end{aligned}
$$
